targets.evidence_quote: A previous study with Virtual Reality (VR) and online motion-capture quantified this approach bias towards food and non-food cues in a controlled VR environment with hand movements. The aim of this study was to test the specificity of a manual approach bias for high-calorie food in grasp movements compared to low-calorie food and neutral objects of different complexity, namely, simple balls and geometrically more complex office tools.
targets.outcome_quote: The results confirm the presence of bottom-up advantages in motor-cognitive behaviour for high-calorie food in a non-clinical population.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Abstract states the earlier approach bias and confirms the corresponding high-calorie approach advantage. Citation unavailable in abstract.
